title: The Predator Principle — The Cancer of Evolution
description:
An open, falsifiable systems hypothesis: predation generalised into the order of everything is the cancer of evolution — and cancer is treatable.

The project distinguishes ecological predation, which can regulate populations and maintain diversity, from a detached system pattern that persistently combines asymmetric extraction, externalised harm, suppressed feedback, compulsory escalation and erosion of its own substrate. Competition is neither rejected in advance nor made the goal; it is assessed by its actual system effects.

Every public claim carries its evidence status — E for empirical evidence, I for interpretation, P for a proposition still to be tested — together with its boundary and the conditions that would falsify it. The strongest objection to the thesis is published alongside it. Counterevidence is explicitly invited through the public issue tracker.

This release contains the essay corpus, the claim and source registers as machine-readable JSON, the published dispatches, and the automation that keeps them in sync.
